item.title: [ZEPPELIN-1263] Should specify zeppelin's spark configuration through --conf arguments of spark-submit
item.description:
For now, we load zeppelin's spark configuration at runtime in the RemoteInterpreter Process rather than loading them before starting the process (through --conf of spark-submit). It is fine for most of spark configuration, but for some configuration, it would introduce some weird issues. Like ZEPPELIN-1242, and if you specify spark.master as yarn-client in spark-defaults.conf but specify spark.master as local in zeppelin side, you will see the spark interpreter fail to start due to this inconsistency. Another case is that spark.driver.memory won't take effect.
So I propose to specify zeppelin's spark configuration through --conf arguments of spark-submit

status.description: A resolution has been taken, and it is awaiting verification by reporter. From here issues are either reopened, or are closed.

comments.comment:
Thanks for the suggestion.

So far, interpreter process runs through bin/interpreter.sh and properties are not passed to bin/interpreter.sh.
How do you think Zeppelin can configure spark through --conf argument of spark-summit?
For now, user can set by setting args, right?
I mean to pass properties to bin/interpreter.sh via environment variable if the properties are spark properties. --conf can override spark-defaults.conf correctly. Do you have any concern on this ?

One my concern is the value of environment variable that holds properties can become long. And some OS (windows) has short limitation.

Another concern is, we want to minimize specialized code for spark in the interpreter abstraction layer and want to make it generalized as much as possible. I know we already have some specialized code in bin/interpreter.sh for spark, but if there're some way to make it generalize, that would be better.

And spark seems read JVM properties starting with spark.*, too. I'm not sure, but if JVM properties are treated exactly same to --conf argument, how about thinking about exposing all properties into JVM properties of interpreter? that would be more generalized approach. (still need to find a way to pass long variable to interpreter.sh)

Do you concern about the length of driver-class-path and driver-java-options ? I would not do it for these 2 configurations. What I would like to add is the spark properties in the interpreter setting page. By default I only see 4 configuration that I need to pass through --conf,

  • master
  • spark.app.name
  • spark.cores.max
  • spark.executor.memory

Users can add spark specified properties in the interpreter setting page, but even that I think it is very rare to reach the limitation of enviroment variable length. Even it reaches the limitation, we can detect that and fail the spark interpreter before launching it.

Actually I think passing spark configuration through --conf is a more general approach. For now, I see some duplicated code in SparkInterpreter.java which should be handled by spark as long as pass right configuration to spark. Let me first prepare a PR for it, then it may be more clear to you.

GitHub user zjffdu opened a pull request:

https://github.com/apache/zeppelin/pull/1446

ZEPPELIN-1263. Should specify zeppelin's spark configuration through --conf arguments of spark-submit

      1. What is this PR for?

For now we spark configuration at runtime rather than pass them through `--conf`, it would cause several issues.

  • Some configuration has to be set through --conf, otherwise we need to duplicate code in SparkSubmit.scala (spark.yarn.keytab, spark.yarn.principal)
  • Some configuration would conflict with spark-defaults.conf. If you specify spark.master as yarn-client in spark-defaults.conf but specify spark.master as local in zeppelin side, you will see the spark interpreter fail to start due to this inconsistency.
  • As ZEPPELIN-1460 described, it is hard to figure what is the effective configuration.
  • We can not use yarn-cluster mode although it is not supported now, but I think it is necessary to do that as zeppelin needs to support multiple users.

So this PR would pass all the spark related configuration to spark-submit through `--conf`, so that it is easy to know and guarantee that configuration on zeppelin interpreter setting take precedence over spark-defaults.conf. And it is also good for maintenance that upstream change (any change about configuration in spark) would not affect us.

I agree on the direction of this PR. But on the implementation I wish we try keep `class RemoteInterpreter` interpreter independent as much as possible.

This PR adds spark specific code to `RemoteInterpreter.getEnvFromInterpreterProperty()`.
And we used to have spark specific code in `bin/interpreter.sh`.

In the future, it'll be better if we provide generic facility in both `bin/interpreter.sh` and `class RemoteInterpreter` and move all spark specific code into spark interpreter module.

Other than that, LGTM.
